title: How can I use autotiles in photoshop?

posts.author: Danatoth
posts.body: I'm making parallax maps in photoshop with a resized version of a tileset. However, some of the tiles are autotiles so I can't use them in photoshop in the same way I can just drag and draw in rpg maker. I'm wondering if there is a way to use them inside of photoshop?

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Your choice of tool seems suspect. Can you even drag and draw with regular tiles in Photoshop? I would have expected that to create a blurry mess.
I don't think you're likely to find something that'll let you "drag and draw" autotiles in Photoshop – one specific piece of the autotile, maybe, but not automatically selecting the right piece for a given location. If that's what you want, you may want to try using Tiled for this instead. With a bit of initial setup, you can draw your map almost exactly how you would in RPGMaker, and then you can export it to an image to use as a parallax.
There's also the possibility of just doing this straight in RPGMaker instead of using a parallax. If your tileset is resized to exactly twice the dimensions, it might be possible to rework the autotiles so they still look okay. Though, that'd probably require editing pixels to avoid hard seams (because you need to find a way to fit the scaled-up graphics into the same size as the original graphics, which obviously means you need to cut parts of it out).

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
I agree with the answer above, but if you still want to use autotiles here is how.
An autotile is basically a collection of 20 quarter-tiles, and the RM-engine has a logic that changes which four of those quarter tiles are used for any tile placed depending on which of the eight tiles next to it is the same autotile or not.
So to use an autotile in any regular image program that does not contain the same automatic, you'll have to divide it into the smaller quartertiles and use them as you would use a regular tile, fitting everything together.

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
autotiles can be used in PS with little editing first
16 pixel from the left + 24 pixels in center (this is looping) and 16 pixels
from the right.
once you have this, you can relative do what you want.
however, loopings as animated is not doable as parallax at all.
this should be open spot and use a plugin that set you a layer below parallax
to make this work
or paint it as autotiles on top op the parallax (what most do).
fallen lorelei has a tutorial about parallax with a plugin.
but the plugin is usage can be a different one as well.
